relevance_reason: Identifies DNAAF3 mutations in the original CILD2-linked consanguineous families, establishing DNAAF3 as the CILD2 gene, with clinical, ultrastructural and functional data.

findings.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) noted that DNAAF3 (previously C19orf51) on chromosome 19q13 lies within the CILD2 locus mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families with immotile cilia and absent outer dynein arms; affected individuals in 2 of the 3 originally linked families showed large regions of marker homozygosity across the DNAAF3 locus.
quotes: The DNAAF3 gene resides within a previously described PCD locus (CILD2 locus; MIM 606763) mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families characterized by immotile cilia with absent ciliary outer arm dyneins.
both of which display large regions of marker homozygosity across the DNAAF3 locus in affected individuals

findings.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) studied 10 patients from 3 consanguineous families (2 Arabic-origin families and a UK-Pakistani first-cousin family) with PCD due to DNAAF3 mutations, presenting with neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge, chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps and bronchiectasis. Four of the 10 had situs inversus. Electron microscopy showed reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms, and nasal cilia were immotile in all affected individuals; the authors noted the disorder was associated with male infertility.
quotes: All the PCD families reported here presented with classic clinical symptoms that included neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge and chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps and bronchiectasis.
Four out of the 10 affected individuals have situs inversus (Fig. 2).
Furthermore, cilia in nasal brushing biopsies were immotile in all affected family members (Supplementary table 2).
giving rise to classical PCD associated with defective left-right organ asymmetry and male infertility

phenotypes.text: absent inner and outer dynein arms
phenotypes.hpo_label: Absent inner and outer dynein arms

findings.statement: In affected members of consanguineous Arabic-origin family UCL89 with CILD2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.323T>C transition in exon 3 of DNAAF3, resulting in a leu108-to-pro (L108P) substitution at a highly conserved residue. The variant was absent from 148 population-matched Arabic control chromosomes and from dbSNP, 1000 Genomes and NHLBI-ESP, was predicted probably damaging, and segregated with recessive inheritance (parents and unaffected sibs heterozygous).
quotes: Two different mutations were detected: c.323T>C in exon 3 creating missense mutation p.Leu108Pro in family UCL89, and c.406C>T in exon 4 creating nonsense mutation p.Arg136X in family UCL66/67 (Fig. 2b). Neither variant was present on 148 population-matched control Arabic chromosomes.
The p.Leu108Pro mutation was predicted with 100% confidence to be ‘probably damaging’ using Polyphen2 and SIFT, and is highly conserved across ciliated species (Fig. 2c).
all affected individuals carried homozygous mutations while unaffected parents and siblings carried heterozygous changes consistent with recessive inheritance

findings.statement: In affected members of Arabic-origin family UCL66/67 with CILD2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.406C>T transition in exon 4 of DNAAF3, resulting in an arg136-to-ter (R136X) nonsense substitution. The variant was absent from 148 Arabic control chromosomes and from dbSNP, 1000 Genomes and NHLBI-ESP, and unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous.
quotes: Two different mutations were detected: c.323T>C in exon 3 creating missense mutation p.Leu108Pro in family UCL89, and c.406C>T in exon 4 creating nonsense mutation p.Arg136X in family UCL66/67 (Fig. 2b). Neither variant was present on 148 population-matched control Arabic chromosomes.
None of these mutations are present in the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes or NHLBI-ESP polymorphism databases.

findings.statement: Among 112 additional PCD families screened, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that affected members of a first-cousin UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) showing linkage to the chromosome 19 locus carried a homozygous 1-bp insertion in exon 6 of DNAAF3 (c.762_763insT), predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (p.Val255CysfsX12). The variant was absent from 172 UK-Pakistani control chromosomes and segregated with the disorder.
quotes: one family showing evidence of linkage (UCL71, Fig. 2a) had a homozygous single basepair insertion within DNAAF3 exon 6, c.762_763insT, creating a predicted frameshift that generates 11 novel amino acids after a p.Val255Cys change followed by a premature stop codon (p.Val255CysfsX12)
UCL71 is a first-cousin union UK-Pakistani family and this variant was absent from172 control UK-Pakistani chromosomes.

findings.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) found a homozygous c.973G>A (p.Ala325Thr) variant in DNAAF3 in a Belgian PCD patient, but considered it likely a Caucasian polymorphism because it was found on 1 of 192 Caucasian control chromosomes, was predicted benign, and affected a nonconserved residue.
quotes: An additional homozygous single basepair substitution (c.973G>A) identified in a Belgian patient (OP-549) creates a missense variant, p.Ala325Thr. However, one of 192 Caucasian control chromosomes carried this variant, which is predicted as ‘benign’ using Polyphen2 and SIFT.
This residue is not conserved and this variant is likely to be a Caucasian polymorphism.

findings.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) found by immunofluorescence that outer dynein arm components DNAH5, DNAH9 and DNAI2 and the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 were absent from respiratory cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations, with residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 in the apical cytoplasm in some patients, suggesting that DNAAF3 is required for cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire axoneme.
quotes: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.
In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 can be seen in the apical cytoplasm, whereas cytoplasmic accumulation of these proteins is not seen in control samples.

findings.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant, carrying a nonsense mutation (p.Trp79X) in the DNAAF3 ortholog, had paralyzed half-length flagella lacking outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms b and c; PF22 was exclusively cytoplasmic. In pf22 cytoplasm, IC2 was hyperabundant and heavy chain-intermediate chain complexes formed abnormally, suggesting PF22 acts at a later step of dynein preassembly than PF13 and ODA7.
quotes: The Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant DAB1 gene has a single G to A base change in exon 3 at codon 79, TGG -> TGA, altering a tryptophan to a nonsense codon (p.Trp79X)

Cell fractionation showed that the MycPF22 protein migrates as a 60 kDa band in cytoplasmic fractions, whereas no equivalent band was seen in axonemal fractions even when loaded at a 50X stoichiometric excess
if PF22 acts as a co-chaperone, it likely works at a later step than PF13 and ODA7 such as the stabilization of heavy chains or the joining of heavy chains and smaller subunits into a larger complex

findings.statement: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that morpholino knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish caused immotile olfactory placode cilia with reduced or missing dynein arms, body axis curvature, hydrocephalus, pronephric cysts, otolith defects, and left-right patterning defects, with about half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos showing reversed or absent heart looping.
quotes: Abnormal body axis curvature, with the downward-curving tail (Fig. 5a, b) typical of zebrafish with defects in cilia motility - or assembly was observed in 64% of dnaaf3MOex3 and 78% of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos.
Hydrocephalus was also present in 18% of dnaaf3MOex3 and 34% of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos
with about half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos exhibiting either reversed or no heart looping (Fig. 5g)

relevance_reason: Reports a genome scan in Arabic families that maps a PCD locus to chromosome 19q13.3-qter (the CILD2 locus) and confirms locus heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) performed a genome scan in 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Using GENEHUNTER, they obtained a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7. Recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218 defined a 15-cM critical region.
quotes: A genome scan was performed in five Arabic families. Using GENEHUNTER, a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 was obtained on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7.
A 15 cM critical region is defined by recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218.

findings.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) stated that their data gave significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirmed locus heterogeneity. The estimated proportion of linked families was 0.7.
quotes: These data provide significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirm locus heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Meeks et al. (2000) described primary ciliary dyskinesia as an autosomal recessive condition with chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. They reported that situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome) and that the estimated incidence is 1 in 20,000 live births. They stated that the condition is caused by defective ciliary function with ultrastructural abnormalities, including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation.
quotes: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome).

The clinical phenotype is caused by defective ciliary function associated with a range of ultrastructural abnormalities including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Absent respiratory ciliary axoneme radial spokes
